clue.text: Smell hung over town

parts.note: BO is short for body odour, a bad smell
someone hung over feels rough

explanation.surface: A bad smell hangs over a town like a cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is an administrative town or district with its own council.

clue.text: Shy hit near maximum

parts.note: to bash is to hit

indicators.note: near means nearly all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: full means at its maximum

explanation.surface: A timid player hits the ball almost as far as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Bashful means shy and easily embarrassed.

clue.text: Win from evil by working miracle

indicators.note: working, like dough being worked, signals the letters being reshaped

explanation.surface: A preacher saves a soul from wickedness by performing a miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim someone is to rescue them from vice or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Make one sir, as Tarzan might be heard to say

indicators.text: as Tarzan might be heard to say
indicators.note: Tarzan speaks in broken English, so the phrase is what his speech sounds like

parts.note: to sir someone is to make him a knight; Tarzan would say you knight

explanation.surface: Tarzan, in his famous broken English, tries to knight a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarzan's pidgin ('me Tarzan, you Jane') for dubbing someone sir would be 'you knight', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to join them so they make one whole.

clue.text: It steers worker to the French watering hole

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
le is French for the
a bar is a place to drink, a watering hole

explanation.surface: A labourer is guided to a French pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Handlebars are the bar a cyclist holds to steer the bike.

clue.text: Directly opposed including backup in demand

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it, so including signals a container

parts.note: polar opposites are directly opposed
read as back-up: the word up written backwards gives PU

explanation.surface: Opposing views get included as a fallback when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backup' has to be read as two words, back + up, so the word up is written backwards; 'including' then puts that inside the word for directly opposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something popular is widely liked and so much sought after.

clue.text: Bird exercises judgment

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercises
wit can mean good sense or judgment

explanation.surface: A bird makes careful decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: The pewit (peewit) is the lapwing, named for its call.

clue.text: China's almost swinish about booze-up

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second
almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: porcine means like a pig
booze is ale, written up the page (backwards) in this down clue

explanation.surface: Chinese revellers behave like pigs at a drinking party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts PORCINE to PORCIN, which goes 'about' ELA (ALE read upwards).
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine ceramic ware, also called porcelain.

clue.text: Where John's at hand in military formation

indicators.note: the middle letters sit inside the formation word

parts.note: troops drawn up in a line
R for right, as in right hand

explanation.surface: A soldier named John stands ready in the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a person but is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a toilet, especially in a camp; john is slang for one.

clue.text: Lake, on reflection, inhabited by oriental animal

indicators.note: the first piece has the second living inside it

parts.note: lake is a red pigment, so red, and its mirror image der, together give these letters
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: An eastern creature lives in a lake seen as a reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake is not water but crimson lake, a red dye; RED with its mirror image beside it gives REDDER, and E goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large animal, the biggest British deer.

clue.text: Notices division?

parts.note: a newspaper is divided into parts, one of which carries the notices

explanation.definitionFit: A section is a division or part of something, such as the notices part of a paper.

clue.text: Stuff stuffed

definitions.meaning: stuff is an old word for woollen cloth, and this fabric is a fine woollen yarn
stuffed in the slang sense of beaten or defeated

explanation.definitionFit: Worsted is a woollen fabric (stuff), and to be worsted is to be beaten (stuffed).

clue.text: Possible producer of wind instrument

definitions.meaning: a kind of bean, and beans notoriously cause flatulence
the same word names a small flute-like woodwind

explanation.definitionFit: The flageolet is both a French haricot bean and a small fipple flute.

clue.text: Best French star makes comeback nonetheless

indicators.note: coming back means the remaining letters are read from right to left
none means nothing, the letter O, and less means it is taken away

parts.note: etoile is French for star

explanation.surface: A top French celebrity returns to the stage regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' is read as none-less: O (nothing) is dropped from ETOILE to leave ETILE, which 'makes comeback' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, the pick of the bunch.

clue.text: I'm within settled restriction

indicators.note: the first word's letters are placed inside the second piece

parts.note: a bird that has settled on a branch has lit (alighted)
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone says they are working inside an agreed restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a restriction or boundary that may not be exceeded.

clue.text: Wedding outfit depicted by artist (Theodore, not Henri)

indicators.note: not Henri tells us to use the initial of Theodore, the other Rousseau, rather than Henri's

parts.note: Theodore Rousseau was a French landscape painter

explanation.surface: A bridal gown appears in a painting by the lesser-known Rousseau.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Henri and Theodore Rousseau were French painters; 'not Henri' says to use Theodore's initial in front of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride collects for married life.

clue.text: Rover's whelp returned stick to the Queen

indicators.note: returned means the word is sent back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a whelp is a young animal, a cub
a cane is a walking stick
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A dog called Rover brings a puppy back and a stick to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover looks like a dog's name but means a sea rover, a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover in the old sense is a pirate, the same as a buccaneer.

clue.text: Said to be a dying insect?

definitions.text: Said to be a dying insect?

parts.words: Said to be a dying insect?
parts.note: dying said aloud is dyeing: an insect crushed for colouring cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a scale insect and the red dye made from it.

clue.text: See one's spring in broken crib

indicators.note: the middle pieces go inside the rearranged letters
something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: one is I, and 's is short for is: I plus S
to hop is to spring or jump

explanation.surface: Someone sees a baby's spring inside a broken cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the crib letters and 'in' puts the rest inside them. A see is the area a bishop has authority over.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the diocese or office of a bishop, which is also called a bishopric.

clue.text: Material made by beastly males

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Animal husbandry produces the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding and tailoring.

clue.text: Bad-mouth topless Tahitian, for example

indicators.note: the top letter of this down word is removed

parts.note: a Tahitian is an islander from Tahiti

explanation.surface: Someone insults a Tahitian woman sunbathing topless.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander is to bad-mouth someone with false statements.

clue.text: Interminably wind from the east, returning to central point

indicators.note: returning means the letters run back the other way
without its termination, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: the levant is an easterly wind of the western Mediterranean

explanation.surface: An endless easterly wind keeps blowing back to the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminably' drops the final T of LEVANT to leave LEVAN, which 'returning' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel is the belly button, used figuratively for a central point or hub.

clue.text: Corpse that crosschecks?

parts.note: a walking corpse is held in check by a crucifix

explanation.definitionFit: A vampire is an undead corpse, traditionally repelled by a cross.

clue.text: It's got from flax backed over bearings

indicators.note: the first piece sits over the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a coat backed with fabric is lined
S and E, the compass points south and east

explanation.surface: Flax products are stacked over a compass bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed is the seed of the flax plant.

clue.text: Menswear?

parts.note: read as men's wear, it suggests clothing; it also hints at men themselves, informally called fellows

explanation.definitionFit: Chaps are leather leggings worn by cowboys, and chaps is also slang for men.

clue.text: One who works at moving lines on map isn't sacked

definitions.text: One who works at moving lines

indicators.note: a place that is sacked is plundered and thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cartographer is told the lines on the map are not right and is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving lines' sounds like map work but refers to railway lines switched at points.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointsman operates railway points, which move trains from one line to another.

clue.text: Group of lawmen have last ship scuttled

indicators.note: a scuttled ship is sunk, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to have is to possess
SS stands for steamship; the last pair goes

explanation.surface: Sheriff's men are told to sink the last boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Ruff at rear end of body

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the rump is the hind end of a body

explanation.surface: A frilly collar sits at the back of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruff is not the collar: in card games, to ruff is to trump.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge and whist, to ruff means to play a trump card.

clue.text: Put right about clothing

parts.note: re means about or concerning
dress means clothing

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a remark about what people wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to put it right or remedy it.

clue.text: Learned it in coarse English first

indicators.note: first places the letter for English at the very front
one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: coarse means rude or vulgar

explanation.surface: A scholar picked up some vulgar English before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (with two syllables) means scholarly and well read.

clue.text: Top brand of car's close to invincible

parts.note: a marque is a make of car

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A leading car brand is very nearly unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: Top is not 'best' here: a big top is a circus tent, like a marquee.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent, and a big top is the circus kind.

clue.text: Bush talk for "see!"

parts.note: George Bush senior famously said read my lips, meaning see what I am saying

explanation.definitionFit: To lip-read is to understand speech by watching the movement of the lips.
